name: Mailpit
description: A mail-testing server: an SMTP listener that keeps every message it is sent, and a web inbox to read them in, with an API for test suites. Nothing is delivered anywhere.

access.note: Mailpit's inbox has no login of its own: anyone who reaches this address reads every captured message. Its own web-interface authentication takes a user:password pair in one variable (MP_UI_AUTH), which this dashboard cannot compose from a generated secret, so protect the domain with the dashboard's password protection or restrict who may reach it. The SMTP listener on 1025 is not published; programs on this server's Docker networks send to it by the container's address, and anything else can post messages through the HTTP API (/api/v1/send) behind the domain.

inputs.name: domain
inputs.label: Public domain
inputs.description: Optional; the address other people open; nothing else here changes when it does.

inputs.name: max-messages
inputs.label: Messages to keep
inputs.description: Older messages are deleted once the inbox holds this many; 0 keeps everything.

ports.name: http
ports.purpose: The web inbox and the HTTP API

ports.name: smtp
ports.purpose: The SMTP listener that captures mail; reachable from containers, never published

volumes.name: data
volumes.purpose: The SQLite database of captured messages

update.notes: Mailpit migrates its message database on start. Captured mail is test data; the backup exists so a redeploy does not empty the inbox.
